pcb_considerations.assertion: Keep the trace from antenna-pin output to connector as short as possible; do not route RF signal across the board; keep RF signal away from the SIM card and power ICs.
Make the VBAT positive line short and wide; route source to VBAT through Zener diode then large capacitor; make pins 36 and 37 as short a connection as possible to power-source ground.
The module has 23 GND pads; if possible, do not route signals on the upper layer of those pads.
Keep SIM-card holder away from antenna/RF cable and near the module; use ESD protection for SIM_CLK, SIM_DATA, SIM_RST, and SIM_VDD; keep them away from power and high-speed-frequency signals.
Keep audio traces away from antenna and power and avoid routing them in parallel with VBAT trace.
Route UART signals together, and likewise USB signals.
For power design, PCB traces from VBAT pins to supply must be at least 60mil wide; place the power IC and bypass capacitor as close to the module as possible.
SIM traces should be short, away from RF/VBAT/high-speed lines, and the holder ground should connect directly to main ground; shield SIM signals with ground.
Audio lines should be routed as differential signals; keep them away from RF cable, antenna, and VBAT. Place one group of audio bypass capacitors near the module and another near the connector.

antenna_requirements.assertion: Three antenna interfaces are provided: GSM_ANT, BT_ANT, and FM_ANT.
Antenna input impedance should be 50Ω and VSWR should be less than 2.
Place GSM and BT antennas as far apart as possible; isolation between the two antennas should exceed 30dB.
GSM_ANT can connect to the module using a 50Ω microstrip line or stripline antenna.

For GSM matching, values of R101/C101/C102 are set by antenna design; normally R101 is 0Ω and C101/C102 are not mounted. The RF connector used for conducted RF test should be as close as possible to the antenna pin; component-to-component trace impedance must be controlled to 50Ω.
For BT matching, values of R201/C201/C202 are set by antenna design; normally R201 is 0R and C201/C202 are not mounted.
Keep the antenna matching circuit close to the antenna, maintain 50Ω RF traces, and keep RF traces away from high-frequency signals and strong interference sources.
For the FM antenna circuit, normally R301/R302 are 0Ω and C301/C302 are not mounted; the earphone-GND option normally uses R301=0Ω with C301/C302/L301 not mounted.

protection_circuits.assertion: For VBAT, the document strongly recommends a 100uF low-ESR tantalum CA, 1uF–10uF ceramic CB, 33pF and 10pF capacitors, and a 5.1V/500mW Zener diode close to VBAT; the diode is said to prevent surge damage.
All SIM-interface signals should be protected against ESD with a TVS-diode array. The document recommends ESDA6V1-5W6 or SMF05C and locating SIM peripheral components close to the SIM holder.
SIM-design guidance: TVS parasitic capacitance should not exceed 50pF; 51Ω resistors on SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA enhance ESD protection; 22pF capacitors reduce RF interference.
USB data-line TVS capacitance should be less than 5pF and the data lines should be routed differentially.
The GSM antenna D101 is a bidirectional TVS for ESD protection; recommended parts are listed as Murata LXES03AAA1-098, LXES03AAA1-154, LXES15AAA1-153, LXES15AAA1-100, and LXES15AAA1-017.
Speaker and microphone reference figures show ESD protection at the external audio endpoint.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1 second and release. The module says it sends RDY when power-on completes at fixed baud rate; RDY does not appear when autobauding is active.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: RDY is sent at fixed baud rate after completion; this URC is absent with autobauding active.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1.5 seconds and release. The document gives 1.5s<T1<33s and timing relationships, and says the module logs off and saves data before shutdown.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: NORMAL POWER OFF URC before completion; STATUS low indicates power-off mode.

functional.method/procedure: Issue AT+CPOWD=1 for normal power off.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: NORMAL POWER OFF URC before completion; STATUS low indicates power-off mode.

functional.method/procedure: Power off, wait at least 800ms after STATUS becomes low, then power on.
Observe NETLIGHT after power off, before registration, after registration, and when GPRS communication is established.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Off when powered off; 64ms on/800ms off when not registered; 64ms on/3000ms off when registered; 64ms on/300ms off when GPRS communication is established.

functional.method/procedure: Observe pin 42 while powering the module on and off.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: High when powered on and low when powered off.

communication.method/procedure: With autobauding enabled on power-up, send AT, at, aT, or At until the DTE receives OK. DTE serial format must be 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: OK response means DTE and DCE are correctly synchronized.

communication.method/procedure: Power on the module and connect USB_VBUS, USB_DP, USB_DM, and GND to the PC; do not operate PWRKEY during the procedure.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: When USB_VBUS is detected and USB_DP/USB_DM communicate normally, the module enters USB download mode automatically.

communication.method/procedure: The document presents conducted output-power tables for GSM850/EGSM900 and DCS1800/PCS1900 and says they follow 3GPP TS 05.05 technical-specification requirements.
The document states the conducted receive sensitivity table was tested under static condition for GSM850/EGSM900 and DCS1800/PCS1900.

power.method/procedure: Use VBAT=4.0V, CA=100uF tantalum with ESR=0.7Ω, and CB=1uF–10uF; the figure labels a 2A burst.

The source's Table 36 reports current consumption under the listed power-off, sleep, idle, voice-call, and GPRS data-mode conditions; it says values are typical laboratory values and individual production units may differ.

environmental.method/procedure: The ESD table reports contact- and air-discharge results at temperature 25℃ and humidity 45% for VBAT, GND, UART1_TXD/UART1_RXD, antenna port, SPKP/SPKN/MICP/MICN, and PWRKEY.

missing_data.reason: No GNSS or GPS support statement was found in the complete supplied hardware-design source.
The supplied hardware document contains only scattered command references and points to a separate family AT-command manual; that manual was not supplied and would not itself prove per-model support.
The source gives the restart sequence but no explicit acceptance criterion.
The source provides output-power/tolerance tables and states conformance to a 3GPP requirement, but does not express a pass/fail criterion or test procedure.
The source reports sensitivity results under static condition but no explicit pass/fail criterion.
The source identifies the table as typical laboratory values and supplies no acceptance criterion.
No standalone temperature-cycle, humidity, vibration, shock, or thermal validation test procedure is documented in the supplied source.

ambiguities.detail: Table 5's GND pin-number list is line-wrapped such that 31, 66, and 73 are split as adjacent digits in extracted text. Figure 44 corroborates the GND positions. Ground-pin records retain this ambiguity in their citation.

Table 5 says PWRKEY should be low for at least 1 second to power on/down, while the current document's power-off procedure specifies at least 1.5 seconds. The same document's power-on procedure specifies at least 1 second. The JSON keeps each context rather than reconciling them.

Figure 3 is captioned as SIM800C-DS dimensions in mm, but its individual drawing dimensions are not present in the supplied text extraction. The reported 17.6 × 15.7 × 2.3 mm comes from the key-features table, not from reading the drawing.
For AT+CFUN=1 and BS-PA-MFRMS=2, Table 7 reports 1.6mA, whereas Table 36 reports 1.58mA. Both source values are retained separately.

Schematic component labels and connections in the reference-circuit descriptions are transcribed from extracted diagram text. Diagram geometry, unlabelled connections, and component orientation cannot be fully validated from this text-only source.

The pin table names the negative USB signal USB_DM, while Figure 24's extracted schematic text uses USB_DN. This output preserves the pin-table name for the pinout and notes the diagram text without assuming a distinct signal.
